description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.scope: Phase 5 hardening frontend (harden-phase5-ui): the real-stack Playwright suite e2e/stack/ (support.ts and six specs, no route mocks), playwright.stack.config.ts, the wrapper tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs (npm run test:e2e:stack), the mocked suite's testIgnore, ignore files
args.focus: Check against PLAYBOOK Phase 5 (../docs/factory/PLAYBOOK.md: Playwright suites against docker compose, seeds idempotent, self-authored, PII-free) and GATES G5, and the backend stack interface ../scratch/phase5-e2e-stack.md. Pay attention to: tests that could pass vacuously or skip silently; rerun tolerance on an accumulated database (unique content, free mission positions, XP and stats deltas, rank-up state); order independence; the wrapper always taking the stack down (failure, signal) and never touching the owner's compose project doucko or reading backend/.env; the wrapper's verdict never rendering a skipped or not-run suite as PASS; the evidence file's honesty; assertions that pin configurable values; @trace tags only for ids this repo owns (contract/docs/mvp-capability-plan.md); the mocked suite and its npm scripts unchanged; secrets (only the fake committed e2e credentials).

findings.title: Real-stack specs hard-code XP values that FR-34 says are configuration
findings.evidence: FR-34 (contract/docs/requirements.md:116) says the XP values are configuration: 10 / 5 / 1, and each hint costs 2. The specs still hard-code them: practice.spec.ts:62-67 expects `['CORRECT_FIRST_TRY', 10] … ['REVEALED', 1] … ['CORRECT_FIRST_TRY', 8]` and `xp: 19 + bonus`. authoring-to-practice.spec.ts:120 expects `xpAwarded: 10`, and flag-queue.spec.ts:197/202 expects '+4 XP' and `toBe(4)`. The same file avoids pinning the bonus 'configurable, so not pinned here' (line 71), so the suite contradicts itself and breaks if the e2e stack ever runs with a non-default ladder.
findings.suggestion: Work out expected values from the server instead of literals. For example, read the ladder from a config or reference endpoint if one exists, or compare XP in relative terms (first try > revealed, hint reduces by the configured cost) and check that the UI shows `result.xpAwarded` from the attempt response. At the least, keep the literals in one named constant in support.ts that is documented as the e2e stack's configured ladder.

findings.title: The wrapper does not tear the stack down on SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and the SIGINT handler cannot run while spawnSync blocks
findings.evidence: Only `process.on('SIGINT', …)` is registered. A CI cancel (SIGTERM) or closing the console window on Windows (SIGHUP/CTRL_CLOSE) kills node without running `finally { down() }`, which leaves `doucko-e2e` running. All children run under `spawnSync`, so the JS SIGINT handler cannot run until the child returns. If Ctrl+C arrives during `stack('down')`, `up` has already been set to false (line 47), so the handler skips the teardown and the stack can be left half-down.
findings.suggestion: Use async `spawn` with awaited promises so signal handlers can run. Register SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGBREAK as well as SIGINT. Clear `up` only after `down` returns 0, and retry or report a failed teardown.

findings.title: A failed teardown is ignored, and the verdict can still be PASS
findings.evidence: `down()` calls `stack('down')` and discards its exit status. After a green Playwright run, a failed `down` still prints 'Result: PASS', exits 0 and writes an evidence file that says nothing about the stack still running. The `--keep` flag likewise leaves the stack up and the evidence file does not mention it.
findings.suggestion: Record the down status. Put a 'Teardown: ok|FAILED|skipped (--keep)' line in the evidence file and console output, and exit non-zero (or flag the result) when teardown fails.

findings.title: `--keep` is detected anywhere in argv, including Playwright args after `--`
findings.evidence: `const keep = argv.includes('--keep');` searches the whole argv, and `pwArgs = argv.slice(dashdash + 1)` also forwards everything after `--`. So `-- --keep` both keeps the stack up and passes an unknown `--keep` flag to Playwright, which then errors out and gives a FAIL with the stack left running.
findings.suggestion: Parse wrapper flags only from `argv.slice(0, dashdash >= 0 ? dashdash : argv.length)`.

findings.title: Flaky (retried) tests count toward a PASS verdict
findings.evidence: `scope = stats.expected + stats.unexpected + stats.flaky`, and PASS requires only exit 0 and no skips. Under CI (`retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0` in playwright.stack.config.ts:17), a test that failed and then passed on retry is reported as PASS. On an accumulated-state suite that is exactly the order-dependence or rerun-tolerance signal the gate should surface.
findings.suggestion: Report flaky tests in the Result line (for example 'PASS (n flaky)'), or treat `counts.flaky > 0` as FAIL or NOT-EARNED for G5 evidence.

findings.title: The committed G5 evidence was produced from a dirty tree at a commit that predates the suite
findings.evidence: The evidence file says `Frontend commit: 54917ec (working tree dirty)` with `Result: PASS`. 54917ec is the base of this diff and contains none of e2e/stack/, the config or the wrapper, so the PASS is for uncommitted code, not for HEAD dc49cd2. The backend is recorded only by path (`Backend checkout: …`), with no commit hash, so the evidence cannot be reproduced.
findings.suggestion: Re-run `npm run test:e2e:stack` on the committed HEAD and commit the clean evidence file. Have the wrapper also record `git rev-parse HEAD` of DOUCKO_BACKEND_DIR, and ideally refuse PASS on a dirty tree or mark it NOT-EARNED.

findings.title: tasks.md marks items done that have no evidence in the change
findings.evidence: These tasks are ticked `[x]`: '3.3 … findings dispositioned in `review-findings.json`', '3.4 `docs/current-state.md` updated' and '1.1 … record with `--update`'. The diff 54917ec..HEAD contains no review-findings.json, no change to docs/current-state.md and no change to quality/coverage-baseline.json, and this review is still running. '3.1 Two wrapper runs green … the second against the accumulated state of the first' is also doubtful: the wrapper always runs `down` after each run, and support.ts:106 says a down resets the stack ('reset it (tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs takes it down)'). A second wrapper run would then start from a fresh DB, and the evidence file shows only one run. This is the 'done-claims need evidence' lesson in AGENTS.md.
findings.suggestion: Untick 3.3/3.4 until the artifacts exist, or add them. Give each done item an evidence path. Prove rerun tolerance with `--keep` followed by a second run (or a wrapper `--runs 2` mode) and record both runs in the evidence file.

findings.title: The isolation guard rarely runs, so it does not protect against pointing at the owner's stack
findings.evidence: The auto fixture checks the HQ greeting only `if (new URL(page.url()).pathname === '/')` after the test. Most specs end elsewhere: seed ends on /task, stats on /admin/stats, flag-queue on /admin/reports, and admin-session on /admin/tasks. Nothing in playwright.stack.config.ts or the wrapper rejects an `E2E_STACK_URL` that targets the owner's stack before the tests start writing content and XP into it.
findings.suggestion: Add a globalSetup in playwright.stack.config.ts that calls GET /api/child/hq and fails fast unless `displayName === CHILD_NAME` (or a stack marker endpoint/header) before any spec runs.

findings.title: settleRankUp ignores the ack response
findings.evidence: `if (view.pendingRankUp) await page.request.post('/api/child/hq/rank-up-ack', …)` never checks `response.ok()`. If the ack fails (for example a 403/400 on the e2e stack), the leftover rank-up celebration from an earlier run is not cleared. The failure then shows up later as a confusing HQ assertion failure instead of at its cause, and on a fresh DB this path is probably never exercised.
findings.suggestion: Route the call through the existing `json()` helper (or assert `response.ok()`), so a failed ack throws with the status and body.

findings.title: The stats spec assumes the current week does not change mid-test and depends on column positions
findings.evidence: `expect(weekAfter.weekStart).toBe(weekBefore.weekStart)` fails if a run crosses the Europe/Prague Monday 00:00 boundary. `cells.nth(1)`, `cells.nth(4)` and `cells.nth(5)` tie the assertions to column order rather than to column headers, so reordering columns in the stats table breaks the test without any behaviour change.
findings.suggestion: Locate cells by their column header (or by accessible name) rather than by index. For the week boundary, either document the limitation or compare by the `weekStart` of the week that contains the attempt time.

findings.title: Wrapper tears the stack down only on SIGINT, and ignores a failed `down`
findings.evidence: `down()` runs from `finally` and from a `process.on('SIGINT')` handler only. Some ways a run ends never reach either path: a CI job cancel (SIGTERM), closing the console window on Windows (SIGHUP/SIGBREAK), or a `kill` on the node process. Each of these leaves the `doucko-e2e` Postgres, backend and nginx running on 18082 with the fake committed admin password. Separately, `stack('down')`'s exit status is thrown away (line 48), so a failed teardown still prints `Result: PASS` and exits 0 while the stack keeps running.
findings.suggestion: Register the same handler for SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGBREAK (exit 128+n). Record the exit status of `down`. If it is non-zero, add it to the evidence and the verdict (for example FAIL with 'e2e-stack down failed'). Never let a run that failed to tear down return 0.

findings.title: A narrowed run overwrites the G5 evidence with `Result: PASS`
findings.evidence: `-- <playwright args>` is passed straight to Playwright. A run like `-- --grep seed` or `-- e2e/stack/seed.spec.ts` runs 1 test, gets scope 1 and 0 skipped, and is marked PASS. It then overwrites docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md with 'Result: PASS'. Filtered-out tests are not counted as skipped in Playwright's JSON stats, so the skip check does not catch this. The full suite is 21 tests (7 × 3 browsers), but the verdict line looks the same for 1 test or 21. The only clue is the 'Playwright args' line, which a gate or reviewer reading 'Result:' will not check.
findings.suggestion: Before the run, take the expected total from `playwright test -c playwright.stack.config.ts --list` with no filters. If the scope is lower, or `pwArgs` is non-empty, report `Result: PARTIAL` (or NOT-EARNED for G5) and either skip writing `-latest.md` or write the verdict as non-PASS. Only an unfiltered all-projects run should be able to produce PASS.

findings.title: Committed evidence is tied to a commit that does not contain the suite it reports
findings.evidence: The evidence reports 'Frontend commit: 54917ec (working tree dirty)' and '21 passed … Result: PASS'. 54917ec does not contain e2e/stack/ or the wrapper; both arrive in dc49cd2. The PASS therefore cannot be traced to any committed tree, and the suite at HEAD has never been shown to pass on a clean checkout. Under the done-claims-need-evidence lesson, the evidence pointer needs to match the code it vouches for.
findings.suggestion: Rerun `npm run test:e2e:stack` on a clean checkout of HEAD and commit the regenerated file. Optionally make the wrapper refuse PASS (or label it 'unreproducible') when the tree is dirty outside docs/qa and trace.

findings.title: Real-stack specs hard-code XP values that FR-34 defines as configuration
findings.evidence: FR-34 says the XP values (10 / 5 / 1, −2 per hint, floor 1) are configuration, and OQ-4 says they will be tuned after week 1. Even so, practice.spec.ts:39,50,59,62-67,78 assert 10/1/8 and a total of '19 + bonus'. flag-queue.spec.ts:64,69 assert '+4' and a delta of 4, and authoring-to-practice.spec.ts:91 asserts `xpAwarded: 10`. Only the mission bonus is treated as configurable, and even that is required to be `> 0` (line 71). Changing the e2e stack's XP config breaks the suite. flag-queue.spec.ts:48,64 also match hard-coded English toast strings (`/^Nothing changed for/`, `/^Fixed: … \+4 XP/`) instead of using `messages`.
findings.suggestion: Read the ladder from the server, or from an exported e2e-stack config constant, and assert deltas relative to it (first = L1, revealed = Lrev, hint = max(1, L1 − cost), reevaluation = L2 − Lrev). Alternatively, document that the e2e stack pins these values and assert that pin once in one place. Build the toast regexes from `m[...]` keys.

findings.title: Isolation guard runs after the test, so `test:e2e:stack:only` or an overridden E2E_STACK_URL can write to the owner's stack
findings.evidence: `test:e2e:stack:only` (package.json:15) runs the suite against any `E2E_STACK_URL`, without the wrapper. The only isolation check is the auto fixture. It runs after `use()`, i.e. after the test has done its writes, and only if the page ends on '/'. If someone points the URL at the owner's LAN stack (for example after setting E2E_STACK_ADMIN_PASSWORD to get past sign-in), several things happen. Each project's admin-session spec sends a wrong-password login (counting toward any lockout). practice, stats, flag-queue and authoring publish missions, record attempts and add XP to the real child's profile. The guard only fails once that data is already written. `CHILD_NAME` can also be overridden by env, which weakens the check further.
findings.suggestion: Add a Playwright `globalSetup` to playwright.stack.config.ts. It should GET /api/child/hq and abort before any test if `displayName` is not the fixed e2e fake name. Do not let that check be overridden by env. Optionally also refuse any base URL whose port is not the e2e stack's 18082.

findings.title: Stats week comparison fails when a run crosses the Monday week boundary
findings.evidence: The test reads `before.weeks.at(-1)`, practises, then reads `after.weeks.at(-1)` and requires that `weekStart` did not change. If a run crosses Monday 00:00 Europe/Prague, a new week row appears, the before/after deltas compare different weeks, and a correct backend fails the test. This is order-dependent flakiness rather than a security problem, but it affects rerun tolerance.
findings.suggestion: Find the week row by the `weekStart` captured before practising. If `weekStart` changed, retry or skip with an explicit reason that the wrapper counts as NOT-EARNED. Otherwise compare the sum over both weeks.

findings.title: Real-stack suite never checks the NFR-1 authorization boundary or FR-27 answer-key hiding end to end
findings.evidence: Phase 5 is the first time the real nginx → Spring Security → Postgres path is exercised, but no stack spec makes an unauthenticated request to an admin mutation. The only negative check is `GET /api/admin/session` → 401 (admin-session.spec.ts:14,26). seed.spec.ts:29 fetches the child mission payload (`/api/child/missions/{id}`) but never asserts that it contains no `accepted` / answer-spec fields. If nginx routing or a security-config regression exposed `/api/admin/**` writes, or put answer keys into child DTOs, this suite would stay green.
findings.suggestion: Add a stack spec that uses a fresh, unauthenticated `request` context. It should assert 401/403 for POST /api/admin/tasks, PUT …/status and POST /api/admin/sources, and 403 for a signed-in write sent without X-XSRF-TOKEN. It should also assert that the child mission and task JSON contain no `accepted`, `spec` or answer fields before reveal. Tag it with ids this repo owns, or have the backend own the NFR-1 trace.

findings.title: Checklist areas reviewed with no issues found
findings.evidence: (1) Authz: there is no server code in scope. Admin writes in tests send X-XSRF-TOKEN taken from the session cookie. The rank-up-ack POST to /api/child/hq without a token is the child (no-login) endpoint, as designed. (2) Auth/session: tests use only the fake committed `e2e-admin-password-not-secret`, overridable by env, and no real credential appears. (3) Injection: the wrapper uses `spawnSync(process.execPath, args)` without a shell, and test paths are built from server-issued UUIDs. (4) Exposure: the base URL defaults to 127.0.0.1:18082. (5) Privacy/legal: the child name is the fake 'Testovací žák', PDFs come from `makePdf` blank pages, all prompts are self-authored arithmetic, and test-results-stack/ and playwright-report-stack/ are git- and docker-ignored. (6) Secrets: no VITE_* variables were added, and the wrapper only spawns the backend's tools/e2e-stack.mjs (it never opens backend/.env or the `doucko` project). (7) @trace ids FR-1/3/9/24/25/26/27/28/30/32/37/40/41/55 and NFR-6/9 are all frontend-owned in the capability plan. The mocked suite is unchanged except for `testIgnore: 'stack/**'`, and the latest mocked run lists no e2e\stack specs. The wrapper never renders an unrun or skipped run as PASS (lines 78-80). Dependencies: package.json adds no dependencies, but `npm audit` could not be run here (permission denied), so dependency advisories were NOT verified.
findings.suggestion: No action needed for these items, apart from running `npm audit` / the Maven advisory check, which this review did not cover.

findings.title: Coverage summary (harden-phase5-ui has skip_specs: true, so the checklist is PLAYBOOK Phase 5 / GATES G5 plus the proposal's What Changes)
findings.evidence: 12 scenarios: 8 implemented, 3 partial, 0 missing, 1 contradicted. Implemented: the Playwright suite against compose (Postgres + backend + nginx), the coverage baseline, self-authored content, PII-free content, the six journeys, NOT-EARNED when the stack is not up or 0 tests run, the mocked suite's testIgnore, and the ignore files. Partial: the wrapper always taking the stack down (signals), the seed's idempotency, and the verdict for a narrowed run. Contradicted: the G5 command `npm run test:e2e # against docker compose`. All @trace ids (FR-1/3/9/24/25/26/27/28/30/32/37/40/41/55, NFR-6/9) are listed for frontend in contract/docs/mvp-capability-plan.md. Only the fake committed e2e credentials appear in the diff.
findings.suggestion: No action needed for this entry. The findings below cover each partial or contradicted item.

findings.title: G5 gate has no mechanism for the real-stack suite: test:e2e stays mocked and gate-status G5 checks coverage only
findings.evidence: GATES.md G5: "npm run test:e2e   # against docker compose". PLAYBOOK Phase 5: "Frontend: Playwright suites against `docker compose up`". In the code, `test:e2e` is still `playwright test` (mocked, `page.route('**/api/**')`). gate-status has `{ g: "G5", desc: "hardening (coverage)", keys: ["coverage"] }`. qa-verify.mjs:115 runs only `test:e2e`. The proposal confirms it: "qa:verify keeps the mocked test:e2e member… the real-stack run is a separate G5 command". Nothing reads docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md or the wrapper's `Result:` line, so G5 can show green without the real-stack suite ever running. That breaks the declared-method-needs-mechanism rule.
findings.suggestion: Change ../docs/factory first: either have G5 and gate-status consume `docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md` (Result: PASS, fresh, commit == HEAD), or change the GATES.md G5 command to `npm run test:e2e:stack`. Then run `npm run factory:install`. Until then, record an explicit waiver.

findings.title: Wrapper does not take the stack down on SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGBREAK; only SIGINT is handled
findings.evidence: Proposal: "always takes it down". The header comment says "also on failure or Ctrl+C". The code only has `process.on('SIGINT', …)`. A CI job cancel (SIGTERM), closing the console window on Windows (SIGHUP) or Ctrl+Break (SIGBREAK) ends Node with its default handler. The `finally { down() }` never runs and doucko-e2e stays up on port 18082. Also, every step uses spawnSync, so the JS handler cannot run while a child process is active. Cleanup during the Playwright run depends on the child dying first.
findings.suggestion: Register the same handler for SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGBREAK. Consider async spawn so signals are handled while a child runs. Add a unit test for the down-on-signal path (mock the stack tool).

findings.title: No pre-flight guard against an overridden target: E2E_STACK_URL, the password or the child name can point the mutating suite at the owner's stack
findings.evidence: Config comment: "Never point E2E_STACK_URL at the owner's stack." Only the `isolation` auto-fixture enforces this, and it runs AFTER `use()`, once the test has already authored sources, tasks and missions and posted attempts and XP. It also only checks when the final URL path is '/'. admin-session, seed, stats and flag-queue all end elsewhere, so for them the check is effectively a no-op. CHILD_NAME and ADMIN_PASSWORD can also be overridden from env (`E2E_STACK_CHILD_NAME`, `E2E_STACK_ADMIN_PASSWORD`). The wrapper passes E2E_STACK_URL through, and `test:e2e:stack:only` has no guard at all.
findings.suggestion: Add a worker-scoped `beforeAll` or globalSetup that GETs /api/child/hq and aborts the run unless displayName equals the fake name. Pin that fake name, not env-overridable. Also refuse non-loopback URLs or ports other than the e2e port unless an explicit opt-in flag is set.

findings.title: A narrowed or filtered run overwrites the evidence file with Result: PASS
findings.evidence: Proposal: the wrapper writes `docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md` and "a run that… skipped tests is NOT-EARNED, never PASS". The code adds all extra args (`-- --project=chromium`, `--grep seed`, `--last-failed`) to `pwArgs` and still sets `result = 'PASS'` whenever `scope > 0` and nothing was skipped. Tests filtered out by --grep or --project are not counted as `skipped`. One-test runs therefore replace the full three-browser evidence and still say PASS. Flaky tests (`stats.flaky`, retries in CI) also count toward PASS. `forbidOnly` is CI-only, so a stray `test.only` locally also gives a partial PASS.
findings.suggestion: If pwArgs is non-empty, set Result to NOT-EARNED (partial), or write to a separate file and leave the G5 evidence alone. Render flaky > 0 as FAIL or as a separate verdict. Set `forbidOnly: true` unconditionally in playwright.stack.config.ts.

findings.title: Evidence file is not tied to the committed tree and does not record the backend commit
findings.evidence: The evidence reads "Frontend commit: 54917ec (working tree dirty)". The suite ran on uncommitted code before HEAD dc49cd2 was created, so the PASS cannot be matched to any commit. It records only the backend checkout path (`C:\projects\school-tutor\backend-phase5-hardening`), not the backend's commit, so the stack that ran cannot be identified. The rule done-claims-need-evidence requires fresh, resolvable evidence.
findings.suggestion: Re-run `npm run test:e2e:stack` on a clean tree at HEAD and commit the regenerated file. Have the wrapper record `git -C <backendDir> rev-parse --short HEAD` and its dirty state. Have the G5 consumer reject evidence that is dirty or older than HEAD.

findings.title: Ticked tasks 3.3 and 3.4 have no artifacts
findings.evidence: `- [x] 3.3 Review gate over the diff; findings dispositioned in review-findings.json`, but the change folder only has proposal.md, tasks.md and .openspec.yaml. Every archived slice has a review-findings.json; this one does not. `- [x] 3.4 docs/current-state.md updated`, but current-state.md is not in the diff and still says "Current phase: Phase 4", "Last completed gate: G3", "Next task: Phase 5 hardening (G5)".
findings.suggestion: Untick 3.3 and 3.4 until review-findings.json exists and current-state.md is updated (Phase 5, G5, with evidence pointers). Treat these ticks as a correction event, as the AGENTS lesson requires.

findings.title: Task 3.1 claims two green wrapper runs, but there is evidence for only one
findings.evidence: `- [x] 3.1 Two wrapper runs green in chromium, msedge and firefox (the second against the accumulated state of the first)`. The wrapper overwrites e2e-stack-latest.md on each run, so only one run (21 passed) is on record. It also calls `down` after every run. Unless the backend's `down` keeps the Postgres volume, which this repo does not show, the second wrapper run started from a fresh database. Rerun tolerance on accumulated state was then never exercised. Only `test:e2e:stack:only` against a kept stack (`--keep`) would exercise it.
findings.suggestion: Prove rerun tolerance with a mechanism, e.g. a wrapper `--repeat 2` mode that runs the suite twice against one `up`, and record both runs in the evidence. Otherwise reword 3.1 to say what was actually run.

findings.title: Practice and flag-queue specs pin configurable XP values
findings.evidence: Gamification spec: "these values SHALL come from configuration" (Scenario "Values are configuration"). The specs hard-code xpAwarded 10, 1 and 8, summary `19 + bonus`, `format(m['child.task.xp'], { xp: 10 })`, and flag-queue's `+4` ("second try 5 − revealed 1"). Only bonusXp is treated as configurable ("configurable, so not pinned here"). A stack running non-default XP config fails these tests even though the product is correct.
findings.suggestion: Keep the pins but name them as the default-config assumption, e.g. a `DEFAULT_XP` constant in support.ts with a comment that the e2e stack runs default config. Or compute the expected UI text from the served AttemptResult.xpAwarded and assert the ladder only through the order of values.

findings.title: Rank-up during a practice journey is not handled on accumulated reruns
findings.evidence: `settleRankUp` acknowledges only a rank-up that is already pending before the journey. TaskScreen shows `RankUpCelebration` from `result.rankUp` mid-journey and does not acknowledge it (RankUp.tsx:26-27). On accumulated reruns XP keeps growing, so at some rerun an attempt crosses a threshold. authoring-to-practice then goes to '/' without settling it. `settleRankUp` also ignores the ack response status, so a failed ack is silent.
findings.suggestion: Assert the ack response is ok. In authoring-to-practice, call settleRankUp before the final HQ visit. Consider a test that explicitly allows an inline celebration during practice.

findings.title: Stats spec: weak session assertion and failure at the week boundary
findings.evidence: `expect(weekAfter.sessions).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(Math.max(1, weekBefore.sessions))` cannot detect a session that went uncounted. `expect(weekAfter.weekStart).toBe(weekBefore.weekStart)` fails when a run crosses Monday 00:00 Europe/Prague. The spec's session rule (30-minute gap, counted in the week of the first attempt) is not used to derive an exact expectation.
findings.suggestion: Assert an exact delta: 0 if the latest attempt before the test was within 30 minutes, else +1, read from the before-snapshot. Or skip with an explicit reason, not a silent pass, when the week rolled over.

findings.title: Seed idempotency is not exercised by the frontend suite
findings.evidence: PLAYBOOK: "Seeds are idempotent, self-authored, PII-free." The wrapper runs `seed` once after each fresh `up`. The seed spec only checks one seed mission, with taskCount 3 at position 1. A second `seed` on the same database, which would show duplicates, never happens on the frontend side.
findings.suggestion: Call `stack('seed')` twice in the wrapper, or in a dedicated check, and assert the HQ still lists exactly one seed mission with 3 tasks. Alternatively, point to the backend's idempotency test in proposal.md.

findings.title: flag-queue spec matches hard-coded English admin copy instead of message keys
findings.evidence: `page.getByText(/^Nothing changed for/)` and `/^Fixed: the attempt on .* is now correct\. \+4 XP added for the child\./`, while the rest of the suite uses `m['…']` and `format()` (NFR-9, externalized strings). A copy edit in messages breaks the test, or lets a renamed string slip through unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Build the expected text from the matching admin.reports.* message keys with format(), escaping it for regex.

findings.title: Stale results.json could be read when Playwright exits early
findings.evidence: `test-results-stack/results.json` is not deleted before the run. If Playwright exits without writing it, the previous run's counts are parsed into the evidence ("Tests: 21 passed…") next to the new verdict. The verdict itself still comes from the exit status.
findings.suggestion: Delete the report file before spawning Playwright. Check that its mtime is later than startedAt before trusting the counts.

findings.title: Specs pin XP values that FR-34 says are configuration
findings.evidence: FR-34 (contract/docs/requirements.md:116) lists 10/5/1 and the hint cost of 2, then says 'All values are configuration.' practice.spec.ts hardcodes xp 10, 1 and 8 (lines 39, 50, 59, 62-67) and the summary total 19 + bonus (lines 78, 84). authoring-to-practice.spec.ts:91-92 hardcodes xpAwarded: 10. flag-queue.spec.ts:64,69 hardcodes '+4 XP' and a delta of 4. Only the completion bonus is left unpinned ('configurable, so not pinned here'), which is inconsistent. If the e2e stack sets the ladder differently, these tests fail even though the behaviour is correct.
findings.suggestion: Read the ladder from the server, the same way bonusXp is handled. Either expose or fetch the config, or derive the expected values from the AttemptResult.xpAwarded responses and assert the relations between them (first try > second try > revealed ≥ 1, hint costs a fixed delta). Alternatively, have the backend stack contract name the ladder as fixed e2e config and reference it here.

findings.title: Wrapper only handles SIGINT; SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGBREAK leave doucko-e2e running
findings.evidence: Only process.on('SIGINT') is registered. With no handler, SIGTERM (CI cancel), SIGHUP (the console window closing on Windows) and SIGBREAK (Ctrl+Break) use the default action and kill Node immediately. The finally block's down() never runs and the stack stays up. Also, all children are spawnSync with stdio inherit, so JS signal handlers cannot run until the child returns anyway. Cleanup on Ctrl+C actually comes from the finally block, not from the handler.
findings.suggestion: Register the same handler for SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGBREAK. Better still, run Playwright with async spawn so signals can be handled during the run. Document that cleanup relies on the finally block, and that a hard kill needs `node tools/e2e-stack.mjs down` run by hand.

findings.title: A failed `down` is ignored: PASS evidence can be written while the stack is still up
findings.evidence: down() calls stack('down') and throws away the exit status. The evidence file and console show no teardown result, so a failed teardown is invisible: the doc claims the wrapper 'always takes the stack down' while the stack may still be running.
findings.suggestion: Record the down status. Add a 'Teardown: ok|FAILED (exit n)' line to e2e-stack-latest.md, print a loud warning, and exit non-zero (or at least don't print a plain PASS) when teardown fails.

findings.title: Narrowed runs (--project, --grep) overwrite the G5 evidence file with PASS
findings.evidence: pwArgs go straight to Playwright, and any non-zero scope with exit 0 counts as PASS. `npm run test:e2e:stack -- --project=chromium --grep seed` writes 'Result: PASS' to docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md with 1 test, replacing the full 21-test, 3-browser evidence. Only the 'Playwright args' line hints at the narrowing. NFR-6 needs all three browsers.
findings.suggestion: If pwArgs is non-empty, mark the result PARTIAL or NOT-EARNED for G5, or write to a separate file. Only a full run (all projects, no filters) should be allowed to write PASS to e2e-stack-latest.md.

findings.title: Flaky (retried) tests count toward PASS
findings.evidence: scope = expected + unexpected + flaky, and PASS needs only exit 0 and no skips. playwright.stack.config.ts sets retries to 1 under CI, so a test that passes only on retry gives PASS. The flaky count shows only in the Tests line.
findings.suggestion: Treat flaky > 0 as FAIL, or at least as not a clean PASS (e.g. 'PASS (n flaky)', exit non-zero in CI). Retries on a real stack with accumulated state can hide order and state bugs.

findings.title: Stats spec breaks if run across the week boundary
findings.evidence: The test reads stats, practises, then checks weekAfter.weekStart === weekBefore.weekStart along with +1 hint and +1 revealed. A run that crosses Monday 00:00 Europe/Prague (or the backend's week zone) fails for a reason unrelated to the feature.
findings.suggestion: Compare by weekStart. Find the row in `before` with weekAfter.weekStart (0 if missing) and assert the deltas against it, rather than assuming the last row is the same week.

findings.title: Pending rank-up is not settled before the seed spec, and settleRankUp ignores failures
findings.evidence: HqScreen renders RankUpCelebration when pendingRankUp is set (src/features/hq/HqScreen.tsx:89). practice and authoring-to-practice call settleRankUp, but stats.spec.ts, which runs last alphabetically and awards XP, does not settle afterwards. seed.spec.ts never settles before clicking the HQ mission card. With one shared database across chromium, msedge and firefox (and across reruns), the seed test can open HQ while a celebration is pending, so its success depends on test order and the rank thresholds. settleRankUp (support.ts:160) also doesn't check the ack response, so a failed ack goes unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Call settleRankUp(page) at the start of seed.spec.ts, or in the auto fixture before every test. In settleRankUp, assert the ack response is ok, e.g. through json(..., 'POST rank-up-ack').

findings.title: The isolation fixture's owner-data check is mostly vacuous
findings.evidence: The auto fixture is described as ensuring 'the page must not show the owner's stack's data'. It only asserts when a test ends on '/'. stats, flag-queue and both admin-session tests end on admin pages, so for them it checks nothing.
findings.suggestion: Make it real: before each test, GET /api/child/hq through baseURL and assert displayName === CHILD_NAME (and that baseURL's port is not the owner's), or narrow the comment to what it actually checks.

findings.title: Evidence file was produced from the parent commit with a dirty tree, not from the reviewed HEAD
findings.evidence: 'Frontend commit: 54917ec (working tree dirty)'. The suite under review was committed afterwards as dc49cd2, so the PASS evidence comes from uncommitted files and does not resolve to the committed code. Under the done-claims-need-evidence rule, evidence should be fresh and tied to the commit.
findings.suggestion: Re-run `npm run test:e2e:stack` on a clean checkout of HEAD and commit the regenerated evidence, so the Frontend commit line names the reviewed commit with no dirty marker.

findings.title: The real-stack verdict is not consumed by qa:verify or gate:status
findings.evidence: The header says it 'Prints the qa-verify contract: Scope / Result', but nothing under scripts/ or factory.config.json references test:e2e:stack or e2e-stack-latest.md (grep finds no matches). The battery still runs only the mocked `test:e2e`. G5's real-stack evidence is therefore not exit-coded by the gate, and `test:e2e:stack:only` can be run without producing any evidence.
findings.suggestion: Wire the stack run, or a freshness and Result check of docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md, into the gate through ../docs/factory (installed files must not be hand-edited). Until then, record in current-state.md that G5 real-stack evidence is checked by hand.

result.reasoning:
The literals are real. practice.spec.ts:39/50/59/62-67 pins 10/0/1/8 and 19+bonus. But under a correctness lens, the claimed defect does not hold.

1. FR-34 (contract/docs/requirements.md:116) gives these numbers in the spec itself: 10 for a correct first try, 5 for second, 1 for revealed, and a hint costs 2 with a minimum of 1. "All values are configuration" means the product code must not hard-code them. It does not stop an acceptance test from checking the specified default ladder. An e2e test of FR-34 that asserts the FR-34 values is testing the requirement as written. Relative-only checks such as "first try > revealed" would be weaker, and would pass even if the server ignored the spec.

2. Nothing in this repo sets a non-default ladder for the e2e stack. A search of yml/yaml/env/json found no XP, hint-cost or bonus overrides. The failure the finding describes ("breaks if the stack ever runs with a non-default ladder") is hypothetical, and it is the right outcome anyway: a changed ladder should fail an acceptance test that pins the spec values.

3. The "self-contradiction" is not one. The mission bonus is left unpinned (line 71) because FR-34 does not give it a number; OQ-4 only says "once per mission, on first completion". The ladder values are pinned because FR-34 does give them. That is a consistent rule: pin what the spec states and leave out what it doesn't.

At most, moving the literals into a named constant in support.ts would be a maintainability nicety. It is not a correctness bug, and it is not major.

The cited code is quoted correctly. `practice.spec.ts:62-67` does pin `[CORRECT_FIRST_TRY,10]`, `[REVEALED,1]` and `[CORRECT_FIRST_TRY,8]`, plus `19 + bonus`, while line 71 leaves the bonus unpinned. Seen through exploitability and reproducibility, though, the claimed problem does not affect any real user or attacker.

1. **Not product code.** These are Playwright specs that run against the dedicated `doucko-e2e` compose stack. The app has no hard-coded XP; the specs only check what the server returns (`result.xpAwarded`, `bonusXp`, HQ totals). No runtime path in the shipped product is wrong.

2. **The values are the specified defaults.** FR-34 itself says 10 / 5 / 1 and 2 per hint, with a floor of 1. "Configuration" means the backend reads them from config; it does not mean an acceptance test may not assert the default ladder. Checking the spec'd numbers on a fixed test stack is valid acceptance testing. Relative checks would actually be weaker: they would miss a backend that awarded, say, 7 for a first try.

3. **The failure is hypothetical and only comes from a deliberate change.** The specs break only if someone reconfigures the e2e stack's ladder. Nothing in `e2e/stack/support.ts` makes the ladder configurable; it only reads the admin password and child name from env. If a maintainer changed the ladder on purpose, a red test would be correct feedback.

4. **The bonus is not a contradiction.** FR-34 sets exact values for the ladder. The mission bonus has no fixed number in the requirements; OQ-4 only says it is paid once per mission. Pinning the defined values and not the undefined one is consistent.

At most, this is a minor maintainability nit: put the ladder in one named constant in `support.ts`. It is not a major correctness defect, and the mechanism cannot occur for a real user.

I read tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs in full. The finding is partly right and partly wrong about how things fail.

**What is correct:** Only SIGINT has a handler (line 51). If no handler is registered for SIGTERM or SIGHUP, Node uses the default action and terminates straight away. The `finally { down() }` block at lines 83–85 never runs, so `doucko-e2e` stays up. This happens when a POSIX CI runner cancels a job with SIGTERM, and when a Windows console window is closed (Node turns that into SIGHUP, and the default action kills the process). So the leaked-stack mechanism is real.

**What is wrong:** The Ctrl+C story is mostly incorrect. The whole script is synchronous, so the SIGINT handler can only run after the top-level code has finished. Having a handler at all stops Node's default "die on SIGINT", and that turns out to be what makes Ctrl+C safe:
- Ctrl+C goes to the whole console or process group, so the child (playwright, or `stack('up')`) gets it and exits.
- `spawnSync` then returns a non-zero status.
- The synchronous code keeps going into `finally`, which calls `down()` while `up === true`.
- Only after that does the queued SIGINT handler run. It sees `up === false`, skips teardown, and exits with 130.

So the claim that "the handler cannot run while spawnSync blocks" is true but does no harm here, because `finally` does the teardown. The "Ctrl+C during `stack('down')` leaves it half-down" case is real only in the narrow sense that an interrupted `down` is not retried. An earlier `up = false` would not have helped either way, because the handler never runs while `down` is in progress. That is a missing retry, not a correctness bug in the handler.

**Fix:** The suggested async `spawn` rewrite isn't needed. Adding `process.on('SIGTERM' | 'SIGHUP' | 'SIGBREAK', …)` handlers is enough to stop Node dying straight away, and then the existing `finally` will run.

**Severity:** This is local or CI dev tooling, the leak only happens on uncommon termination paths, and the stack can be cleaned up by hand with `e2e-stack.mjs down`. The mechanism is partly confirmed, so I'm not refuting it, but I'd downgrade it from major.

I read tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs:44-85. Only SIGINT has a handler, and every child runs under spawnSync. The finding is partly right but overstates its case.

(1) Ctrl+C during up, seed or Playwright does not leak the stack. With stdio 'inherit' in the same console, the child also gets the Ctrl+C and exits. spawnSync then returns a non-zero status, the try block continues, and `finally { down() }` tears the stack down. The SIGINT handler only runs afterwards; by then `up` is false, so it just exits with 130. The handler being blocked by spawnSync does not matter in this flow.

(2) The CI-cancel/SIGTERM scenario cannot happen. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not run this wrapper. It is only `npm run test:e2e:stack`, a local developer command.

(3) Two real cases remain. First, closing the console window on Windows (CTRL_CLOSE → SIGHUP) or killing node outright. Node exits without running `finally`, so the `doucko-e2e` containers stay up, since Docker owns them. Second, a Ctrl+C during `stack('down')`. Line 47 has already set `up = false`, so nothing retries and the stack can be left half-down. Both are reproducible, but neither is likely.

Impact is low. The stack is an isolated, throwaway compose project that does not touch the owner's project. The comment at line 4 says seeding is idempotent, and the wrapper always runs `up` before seeding, so a leftover stack is presumably reused on the next run. I did not read the backend's tools/e2e-stack.mjs to confirm that. The real cost is leftover containers and ports in use on a dev machine, with no data loss or security effect.

The mechanism is valid for console-close and Ctrl+C during teardown, so I'm not refuting it. It should be downgraded from major to minor.

I read tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs and the mechanism is real. In `down()` (lines 45-50), `stack('down')` at line 48 runs and its return value, the spawnSync exit status, is thrown away. The `finally` at line 84 calls `down()`, but nothing it does feeds into `result` or `reason`. So after a green Playwright run, `result` stays 'PASS'. The script writes "Result: PASS" to docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md and the console, and sets `process.exitCode = 0` at line 111, even when teardown failed.

There is no other guard. The `run()` log only records the command line (`$ node tools/e2e-stack.mjs down ...`), not its exit status, so the evidence file can't show a failure. With `--keep`, `down()` does nothing and the evidence file never says the stack was left running. The only trace is that the down line is missing from the log, which is not an explicit record.

The header comment (line 5) promises it "always takes the stack down again", and the code never checks that it did. The SIGINT handler (lines 51-54) also ignores the down status, though it exits 130 anyway.

Why the severity stays minor: a teardown failure doesn't make the test evidence itself wrong. The tests did pass against the real stack. The damage is a leaked compose project and an evidence record that is missing information. The finding stands as written.

I confirmed the mechanism in `tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs`.

- **Teardown status is dropped.** `down()` (lines 45-50) calls `stack('down')` at line 48 and throws away the exit code. `run()` returns `r.status ?? 1`, but nothing checks it.
- **The verdict is fixed before teardown runs.** `result = 'PASS'` is set inside the try block (line 80). The `finally { down(); }` block (line 84) never changes `result` or `reason`. So a non-zero `down` still gives "Result: PASS" on the console (line 110) and `process.exitCode = 0` (line 111).
- **The evidence file doesn't record teardown.** `docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md` (lines 90-106) has no teardown line. The `$ node tools/e2e-stack.mjs down` command does appear in the embedded log, because `run()` pushes it to `log`. Its exit status is not recorded.
- **`--keep` isn't recorded either.** With `--keep`, `down()` does nothing (`!keep` guard). The evidence file shows the Playwright args (`pwArgs`, which come only from after `--`), not `--keep`. Nothing in the file says the stack was left running.
- **The header promise isn't checked.** The header comment (line 5) says the script "always takes the stack down again", but nothing verifies this.

How it can happen: `docker compose down` can fail for ordinary reasons on a Windows dev machine (the Docker daemon hiccups, a container is locked, or the stack tool errors out). The script then prints PASS and exits 0, and nothing shows that the stack is still up.

Why the severity stays minor: the PASS is still a true statement about the tests, because they really did run and pass, so this is not a false-green on the suite itself. The harm is limited to the evidence being incomplete and a leftover `doucko-e2e` stack that could affect the next `up`. The fix suggested in the finding is the right one.

I read the code and the mechanism is real. In tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs, line 21 sets `const keep = argv.includes('--keep')`, which searches the whole argv. Line 23 sets `pwArgs = argv.slice(dashdash + 1)`, which forwards everything after `--` unfiltered to the Playwright CLI (line 67). Nothing checks or strips the arguments in between. So `node tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs -- --keep`, or `npm run test:e2e:stack -- -- --keep` (npm removes the first `--`), sets keep=true and also passes `--keep` to `playwright test`. Playwright's CLI is built on commander, which rejects unknown options, so it exits non-zero. The wrapper then reports FAIL ('playwright exited N'), and `down()` skips teardown because keep is true, so the stack is left running. The only caller is the package.json script `test:e2e:stack`, which passes arguments straight through. I found no guard anywhere else. This needs user error to trigger: the documented usage on line 8 puts `[--keep]` before `--`. That limits the impact, so minor severity is right. The proposed fix (read wrapper flags only from `argv.slice(0, dashdash)`) is correct.

The mechanism is real. At `tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs:21`, `const keep = argv.includes('--keep')` checks the whole argv. Line 23 then forwards everything after `--` to Playwright, and line 67 splices those args into the Playwright CLI call. The script itself sets no guard that would stop `--keep` reaching Playwright. Running `node tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs -- --keep` therefore sets `keep=true`, so `down()` is skipped, and also passes `--keep` to `@playwright/test` cli.js. Playwright's CLI should reject an unknown option and exit non-zero. If it does, `result` becomes FAIL and the stack stays up. I did not check whether `node_modules/@playwright/test` actually rejects unknown options, so the FAIL part is inferred, not confirmed.

Reproducibility is limited, though. It only happens if the user ignores the documented usage (`[--keep] [-- <playwright args>]`, line 8). Through npm (`npm run test:e2e:stack -- --keep`), npm strips the first `--`, so argv is `['--keep']` and everything works. You only hit the bug with `npm run test:e2e:stack -- -- --keep`, or an odd Playwright value like `--grep --keep`. The result is a loud, non-zero FAIL, not a false PASS. A stack left running is what `--keep` asks for anyway. There is no security impact and no corrupted evidence: the report records FAIL honestly. So the finding holds, but it is a robustness nit about misuse, not a real correctness hazard. I recommend a downgrade.

I confirmed the mechanism in the code. In `tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs`, line 71 counts flaky tests in `scope`. Lines 75–80 give PASS when Playwright exits 0, at least one test ran (`scope` > 0) and nothing was skipped. Nothing checks `counts.flaky`.

`playwright.stack.config.ts:17` sets `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0`, and the config has no `failOnFlakyTests`. So under CI, a test that fails once and then passes on retry is marked flaky. Playwright still exits 0, and the wrapper prints `Result: PASS` and exits 0.

The config's own comment says the suite runs against accumulated state and that order "does not matter". A flaky result is exactly the evidence that would contradict that claim, and the gate hides it.

Two things soften this but don't refute it:
1. The markdown report's `Tests:` line does show the flaky count. But the stdout `Scope:`/`Result:` lines that qa-verify reads don't mention it.
2. Locally `CI` is unset, so retries are 0 and no test can be flaky. The issue only shows up in CI.

The path is reachable, nothing else guards against it, and Playwright's defaults don't catch it. Minor severity is right.

I confirmed the mechanism in the code. In `playwright.stack.config.ts:17`, `retries` is set to 1 when `CI` is set. The project really does run with `CI=1`: the review-gate trace says to run `CI=1 npm run qa:verify`, and the slice evidence docs also use `CI=1`. Nothing sets `failOnFlakyTests`.

So when a test fails and then passes on retry, Playwright exits 0 and puts the test in `stats.flaky`. In `tools/e2e-stack-run.mjs:71`, `scope` includes flaky tests. Lines 75–80 then return PASS, because they only fail on a non-zero exit status, zero scope or skipped tests. Flaky tests never count against the result.

The only mitigation is that the flaky count is written to the `Tests:` line of `docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md`. The `Result:` line and the exit code still say PASS (exit 0), and the qa-verify contract reads that line.

Under the project's own rule (the verdict comes from exit-coded checks), an order-dependent failure on the accumulated-state stack would pass G5 without being flagged. This affects how reliable the gate evidence is, not security. No user or attacker is exposed, so minor severity is right.

I could not refute this finding. Line 8 of docs/qa/e2e-stack-latest.md literally reads `Frontend commit: 54917ec (working tree dirty)` above `Result: PASS`.

The narrow fact is true: the auto fixture at `e2e/stack/support.ts:32` only checks the greeting when the test ends on `/`, and `playwright.stack.config.ts` has no globalSetup. But the finding's actual claim is wrong: it says nothing stops a misdirected `E2E_STACK_URL` before the suite writes content and XP into the owner's stack. Something does.

1. **Every spec that writes signs in first with the fake password.** stats, practice, flag-queue and authoring-to-practice all call `signedIn(page)` before doing anything else (`stats.spec.ts:10`, `practice.spec.ts:18`, `flag-queue.spec.ts:16`, `authoring-to-practice.spec.ts:22`). `signedIn` signs in with `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, which defaults to the fake `'e2e-admin-password-not-secret'`, and then waits for the admin home heading (`support.ts:50-53`). Against the owner's stack the password is rejected, the heading never shows, and the test fails before any write.

2. **Child XP can only come from content those specs author.** The child answers tasks from `publishedMission()`, and that needs the admin session through `adminApi` and an XSRF cookie (`xsrf()` throws without one). So no XP is written unless the admin login succeeded.

3. **The seed spec checks the child's name and writes nothing.** `seed.spec.ts:15-16` calls `GET /api/child/hq` and asserts `displayName === CHILD_NAME` first. It is read-only.

4. **admin-session only signs in.** It tries a wrong password and then the fake one, so it cannot write content or XP.

The only way to reach the owner's data is to point both `E2E_STACK_URL` and `E2E_STACK_ADMIN_PASSWORD` at the owner's stack on purpose. The guard is not meant to catch that. The fixture also does exactly what its comment says (it checks any HQ visit), and it was never meant to be the isolation barrier. A globalSetup marker check would be nice defence in depth, but the harm the finding describes is already blocked.

It's true that the auto fixture at `e2e/stack/support.ts:32` only checks when a test ends on `/`, and that `playwright.stack.config.ts` doesn't validate `E2E_STACK_URL`. But the harm the finding describes, "writing content and XP into" the owner's stack, can't happen through the paths it points to.

1. **Every spec that writes signs in first, with a fake password.** flag-queue, practice, stats and authoring-to-practice each call `signedIn(page)` as their first line. `signedIn` uses `ADMIN_PASSWORD = process.env.E2E_STACK_ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? 'e2e-admin-password-not-secret'`. It then requires the admin home heading within 15 s, and if it doesn't appear the test fails. confirmed.title: The wrapper does not tear the stack down on SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and the SIGINT handler cannot run while spawnSync blocks
confirmed.evidence: Only `process.on('SIGINT', …)` is registered. A CI cancel (SIGTERM) or closing the console window on Windows (SIGHUP/CTRL_CLOSE) kills node without running `finally { down() }`, which leaves `doucko-e2e` running. All children run under `spawnSync`, so the JS SIGINT handler cannot run until the child returns. If Ctrl+C arrives during `stack('down')`, `up` has already been set to false (line 47), so the handler skips the teardown and the stack can be left half-down.
